lessons.title: Telling the Time

items.exampleMeaning: It is a quarter past four.
Excuse me, what time is it?

lessons.tip: In Swedish, we say the hour first, followed by 'över' (past) or 'i' (to) for minutes. Remember to use 'halv' for half past the hour.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: What time is it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: It is a quarter past four.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Thanks! What time is it now?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: It is ten past five.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: And what time is it tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: It is half past two.

scenario.partnerRole: You are a local who knows the time.
scenario.learnerRole: You are a visitor asking about the time.
scenario.brief: Fråga om tiden och svara på frågor om klockan.
scenario.goal: You need to learn how to ask and tell the time.

lessons.title: Buying Tickets

items.exampleMeaning: I want to buy a ticket.
Can I have a single ticket?
Excuse me, how much does it cost?

lessons.tip: When buying tickets, use 'en enkelbiljett' for a one-way ticket and 'returbiljett' for a round trip. Always ask 'hur mycket kostar det?' to know the price.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Do you want to buy a ticket?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, jag vill ha en returbiljett.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I want a return ticket.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: How much does it cost?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ursäkta, hur mycket kostar en enkelbiljett?
dialogue.meaning: Excuse me, how much does a single ticket cost?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: A single ticket costs fifty kronor.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: And a return ticket?

scenario.partnerRole: You are a ticket seller at a train station.
scenario.learnerRole: You are a customer buying a ticket.
scenario.brief: Fråga om biljettpriser och köp en biljett.
scenario.goal: You need to successfully buy a ticket.

lessons.title: Common Verbs in Present Tense

items.exampleMeaning: I go by bus every day.
I take the train to Stockholm.

lessons.tip: In Swedish, the present tense is formed by using the infinitive form of the verb. For example, 'åka' becomes 'åker' for 'I go'.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Do you go by bus?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, jag åker buss varje dag.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I go by bus every day.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Do you walk to the station?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I walk there.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Kommer du med mig till museet?
dialogue.meaning: Are you coming with me to the museum?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I am coming with you.

scenario.partnerRole: You are a friend discussing transport.
scenario.learnerRole: You are the friend who uses public transport.
scenario.brief: Fråga om resor och prata om hur ni reser.
scenario.goal: You need to practice using common verbs in the present tense.

lessons.title: Using Time and Transport Together

items.exampleMeaning: Today I am going to Gothenburg.

lessons.tip: Combine verbs with time expressions to create complete sentences. For example, 'Klockan är tre och jag åker till Stockholm.' means 'The time is three and I go to Stockholm.'

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: The time is three.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: I travel to Stockholm today.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: Are you going with me?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Ja, jag åker till universitetet senare.
dialogue.meaning: Yes, I go to the university later.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.meaning: When are we going?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.meaning: We are going tomorrow.

scenario.partnerRole: You are a travel companion discussing plans.
scenario.learnerRole: You are the one making plans.
scenario.brief: Fråga om resor och tid, och planera tillsammans.
scenario.goal: You need to successfully discuss travel plans using time and transport.
